param.name: feature_type
param.dialogReference:
Select the object type the workflow will find or assess.

  • Choose a listed type, such as Buildings, Vehicles, or Debris, to apply its recommended extraction and embedding settings.
  • Choose Custom when you want SAM3 to extract a different object concept. Then provide a Custom SAM3 Text Prompt.

param.name: workflow
param.dialogReference:
Select the analysis workflow. Available choices depend on Feature Type.

  • Feature Extraction: create target features from imagery using SAM3.
  • Embedding Similarity: find post-event imagery areas that resemble the supplied example points.
  • Damage Assessment: compare target features with post-event similarity results and assign image-evidence classes.

param.name: in_target_features
param.dialogReference: Optional target polygons for Damage Assessment. When supplied, feature extraction is skipped and these polygons are used to measure post-event similarity evidence.

param.name: in_aoi
param.displayname: Area of Interest Polygon (Optional; Clips Supplied Targets and Overrides Extent)
param.dialogReference:
Optional analysis boundary.

  • Provide a polygon to limit processing to an area of interest. It also clips any supplied target features.
  • Alternatively, set Processing Extent in the tool Environments. Use this when you do not have an AOI polygon.
  • If both are set, the AOI overrides the Extent environment.

param.name: pre_event_source
param.dialogReference:
Choose the imagery source used to extract target features.

  • Input Imagery: use a raster layer already in the active map. Then select that layer in Feature Extraction Imagery Layer.
  • World Imagery Wayback: use a historical World Imagery release. Then select its release date.
  • This section is used only when the workflow needs target-feature extraction.

param.name: in_pre_event_imagery
param.displayname: Feature Extraction Imagery Layer (from Active Map)
param.dialogReference:
Select the active-map raster layer used for SAM3 feature extraction.

  • Required when Feature Extraction Imagery Source is Input Imagery.
  • Add the imagery to the active map before opening the drop-down list.
  • The parameter remains unavailable when World Imagery Wayback is selected because the selected release supplies the imagery.

param.name: pre_event_wayback_release
param.displayname: Feature Extraction World Imagery Wayback Release
param.dialogReference:
Select the historical World Imagery Wayback release used for feature extraction.

  • Required when Feature Extraction Imagery Source is World Imagery Wayback.
  • Choose a release that represents the imagery from which target features should be extracted.
  • The parameter remains unavailable when Input Imagery is selected.

param.name: in_sam_model
param.displayname: Custom Extraction Model (.dlpk, Optional; Default: Living Atlas SAM3)
param.dialogReference: Optional local deep learning package that overrides the default Living Atlas SAM3 model used for target-feature extraction.

param.name: custom_sam_prompt
param.dialogReference: Text prompt supplied to SAM3 when Feature Type is Custom. Describe the object concept to extract.

param.name: detection_cell_size
param.dialogReference: Output cell size in meters for SAM3 feature extraction. Smaller values can improve detail but increase processing time and GPU memory use.

param.name: post_event_source
param.dialogReference:
Choose imagery for post-event embedding similarity.

  • Input Imagery: use a raster layer already in the active map. Then select that layer in Post-Event Imagery Layer.
  • Current World Imagery: use the current World Imagery service. No layer or Wayback release is required.
  • World Imagery Wayback: use a historical World Imagery release. Then select the post-event release.
  • This parameter is not needed when Existing Post-Event Embeddings is supplied.

param.name: in_post_event_imagery
param.dialogReference:
Select the active-map raster layer used to generate post-event embeddings.

  • Required when Post-Event Imagery Source is Input Imagery.
  • Add the imagery to the active map before opening the drop-down list.
  • The parameter remains unavailable when Current World Imagery or World Imagery Wayback is selected.

param.name: post_event_wayback_release
param.dialogReference:
Select the historical World Imagery Wayback release used for post-event embeddings.

  • Required when Post-Event Imagery Source is World Imagery Wayback.
  • Choose a release that represents post-event conditions.
  • The parameter remains unavailable when Input Imagery or Current World Imagery is selected.

param.name: in_damage_sample_points
param.dialogReference: Provide at least six representative example points. Each point must intersect a unique embedding cell; selected cells define the imagery appearance used by the similarity search.

param.name: online_embedding_model
param.dialogReference: Select the ArcGIS Online embedding model to download and use when a custom embedding model is not provided.

param.name: in_embedding_model
param.dialogReference: Optional local embedding model package that overrides the ArcGIS Online Embedding Model selection.

param.name: gpu_id
param.dialogReference: Identifier of the GPU used by SAM3 and embedding generation. The default is GPU 0.

param.name: batch_size
param.dialogReference: Number of imagery tiles processed per deep-learning batch. Larger values may improve throughput but require more GPU memory.

param.name: grid_size
param.dialogReference: Spacing factor for embedding generation. Leave blank to use the feature-type recommendation, or supply a positive integer to override it. Smaller grids provide finer detail and increase processing time.

param.name: similarity_threshold
param.dialogReference: Minimum embedding-similarity score from greater than 0 through 1. Higher values retain only cells more similar to the example points.

param.name: out_classified_features
param.dialogReference: Required output feature class for extracted features, debris coverage polygons, similar embedding cells, or classified target features. Store outputs in a file or enterprise geodatabase.

param.name: moderate_coverage_threshold
param.dialogReference: Minimum percentage of a target feature covered by similar embedding cells for the Moderate Damage Evidence class. Used only by Damage Assessment.

param.name: high_coverage_threshold
param.dialogReference: Minimum percentage of a target feature covered by similar embedding cells for the High Damage Evidence class. Used only by Damage Assessment and must exceed the Moderate threshold.

param.name: out_target_features
param.dialogReference: Derived output containing the supplied or extracted target features used by the tool.

param.name: out_embeddings
param.dialogReference: Derived output containing polygon embedding cells and BLOB embedding values generated from post-event imagery, or selected existing embeddings.

param.name: out_similar_embeddings
param.dialogReference: Derived output containing post-event embedding cells that meet the similarity threshold for the selected example points.

param.name: keep_intermediate_data
param.dialogReference: Keep generated target features, post-event embeddings, and similar embedding features after successful processing. Clear this option to delete generated intermediate datasets.

param.name: in_existing_embeddings
param.dialogReference: Optional existing embedding feature class with a BLOB embedding field. When supplied, post-event imagery preparation and embedding generation are skipped.

dataIdInfo.idPurp: Extract target features, identify post-event imagery that resembles user-provided examples, and classify target features using image-based damage evidence. The tool supports Feature Extraction, Embedding Similarity, and Damage Assessment workflows using ArcGIS GeoAI tools, SAM3, and supported embedding models.
dataIdInfo.idAbs: Choose a Feature Type first. Workflow choices update for the selected feature type. Feature Extraction creates target polygons from imagery. Embedding Similarity identifies post-event imagery cells that resemble at least six representative example points. Damage Assessment compares target features with post-event similarity cells and assigns image-evidence classes. Results are preliminary and should be reviewed against source imagery and field observations.
